# **Latticewake: Architectural Research and Specification for a Native Apple Silicon Wave-Terrain Instrument**

## **1\. Verified Facts and Foundational Evidence**

The following section presents a comprehensive analysis of wave-terrain synthesis architectures, existing software implementations, digital signal processing methodologies, and software intellectual property law, derived strictly from verifiable primary and academic literature.

### **1.1 Foundational Principles of Wave Terrain Synthesis**

Wave Terrain (WT) synthesis, occasionally referred to in academic literature as Two-Variable Function Synthesis, constitutes a method of sound generation wherein a two-dimensional trajectory scans a three-dimensional virtual topology to produce an audio signal1. Unlike traditional wavetable synthesis, which sequentially reads a single-dimensional buffer, WT synthesis evaluates a terrain function ![][image1] using a trajectory mapped by time-dependent parametric equations, typically ![][image2] and ![][image3]1. The resulting sequence of ![][image4] coordinates forms the output audio signal. First conceptualized by Rich Gold in 1978 and further formalized by Borgonovo and Haus in 1984 and 1986, the technique separates the harmonic control into two distinct domains: the geometric complexity of the path and the topographical complexity of the surface1.  
Changes to the trajectory orbit (e.g., radius, angle, translation) directly modulate the harmonic structure of the output. If the trajectory orbit remains periodic, the resulting waveform will be strictly periodic, functioning as a complex static oscillator1. Conversely, if the trajectory translates across the surface over time, the waveform exhibits continuous morphological shifts, generating dense, time-varying harmonic structures without requiring explicit frequency or amplitude modulation2.

### **1.2 Analysis of Existing Software Implementations**

Contemporary software instruments have implemented WT synthesis using varied computational strategies, ranging from strict mathematical evaluation to image-buffer scanning.  
The open-source synthesizer "Terrain" by Aaron Anderson (version 1.2.2, updated late 2024, https://github.com/aaronaanderson/Terrain) utilizes per-sample mathematical evaluation2. Operating under the GPL-3.0 license, Terrain allows both the trajectory and the terrain to be modulated at audio rates6. It employs parametric continuous paths, such as elliptical orbits, which scan generated sinusoidal or complex geometric terrains2. Terrain introduces a "Meanderance" function, permitting the trajectory to autonomously displace across the terrain to create time-varying spectra. Additionally, it implements a recursive trajectory feedback loop, bounded by a spatial compressor, and relies on up to 16x oversampling to mitigate fold-over aliasing2.  
Conversely, "Image-In" (version 0.2, updated late 2025, https://github.com/odoare/Image-In) by FX-Mechanics is distributed under the LGPL-3.0 license and operates as a polyphonic VST synthesizer9. Instead of mathematical surfaces, Image-In scans static PNG and JPEG image buffers, mapping pixel luminance to audio amplitude9. The scanning path is defined by three independent, elliptical "Readers" whose center (![][image5]), radii (![][image6]), and angle can be modulated by four LFOs and three ADSR envelopes via a modulation matrix9.  
In programmatic environments, SuperCollider provides the WaveTerrain.ar Unit Generator (UGen) (https://github.com/supercollider/sc3-plugins)12. This implementation requires a 1D buffer to represent a 2D grid, flattening the surface Cartesian coordinates such that the reading index is calculated as ![][image7]13. In the VCV Rack ecosystem, modules such as "Imagine" (https://community.vcvrack.com/t/pachde-imagine-new-sound-from-image-module/19845) evaluate image buffers using procedural paths like scanlines and Boustrephon (alternating left-to-right, right-to-left) to generate control voltage (CV) signals rather than direct audio14.

### **1.3 Technique Taxonomy: Terrain Evaluation and Path Families**

The architecture of a WT instrument fundamentally diverges at the terrain evaluation level, presenting two distinct computational paradigms.  
**Terrain Evaluation Methodologies:**

> 1. **Per-Sample Mathematical Evaluation:** The ![][image4] output is calculated via a direct mathematical formula at every audio sample (e.g., ![][image8])13. This paradigm, utilized by Anderson's Terrain, eliminates the need for RAM allocation or memory bandwidth, placing the entire computational load on the processor's Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Because it is calculated analytically, the terrain itself can be modulated at audio rates without requiring buffer recalculation2.  
> 2. **Image and Table Scanning:** The ![][image4] height is fetched from a pre-calculated 2D buffer in memory9. This approach, utilized by Image-In and SuperCollider, requires memory lookups and spatial interpolation to decode pixel values. While it enables the use of arbitrary data (such as photographs or pre-rendered sonograms), the terrain remains static at the audio rate due to the prohibitive cost of redrawing a 2D buffer every sample9.

**Trajectory Path Families:**

> 1. **Parametric Euclidean Orbits:** The trajectory is governed by continuous trigonometric equations. A standard Lissajous orbit defined by ![][image9] and ![][image10] provides cyclic evaluation1.  
> 2. **Procedural Paths:** Common in image-scanning implementations, these include linear scanlines, spirals (acting similarly to a vinyl record read-head), and randomized boundary-bouncing vectors14.  
> 3. **Dynamical Systems and Chaotic Attractors:** Academic literature advocates for moving beyond simple Euclidean shapes by incorporating non-linear dynamical systems into the trajectory1. Iterated functions and quadratic maps describe trajectories in discrete phase space. By using chaotic attractors, the trajectory generates dense, non-repeating harmonic structures that map more closely to the complexity of physical acoustic phenomena1.

### **1.4 Digital Signal Processing Mechanisms**

#### **1.4.1 Interpolation and Aliasing Control**

When evaluating buffered terrains (images or tables), the continuous trajectory coordinates ![][image11] rarely align with discrete integer grid indices. Extracting amplitude values requires sub-pixel interpolation18.

> * **Nearest Neighbor and Bilinear Interpolation:** Nearest neighbor fetching selects the closest integer coordinate, producing extreme step-wise discontinuities that manifest as broadband high-frequency quantization error in the audio output18. Bilinear interpolation computes a weighted average of the ![][image12] surrounding points. While it smooths the step artifacts, the first derivative of the bilinear surface is discontinuous across cell boundaries, which generates fold-over aliasing during high-frequency traversal18.  
> * **Bicubic Interpolation:** Bicubic convolution resolves derivative discontinuities by interpolating a ![][image13] neighborhood (16 points) around the trajectory coordinate18. This method ensures that the surface and its first derivative remain continuous. However, depending on the convolution kernel parameter (often ![][image14]), bicubic interpolation can introduce overshoot or "haloing" at sharp gradients18. In an audio context, this acts similarly to the Gibbs phenomenon, introducing minor resonance near steep waveform edges.

WT synthesis inherently introduces severe aliasing. Because the harmonic spectrum relies on the nonlinear interplay between the trajectory phase and the terrain topology, the exact bandwidth of the output signal is mathematically intractable to predict8. Consequently, analytic bandlimiting techniques (such as MinBLEP or BLIT) cannot be applied. Anti-aliasing must be managed via oversampling6. The engine must evaluate the trajectory and terrain at a multiple of the sample rate (e.g., 4x to 16x), apply a phase-linear or minimum-phase low-pass filter, and decimate the signal back to the host rate2.

#### **1.4.2 DC Offset and Limiting**

Certain topological fields, particularly those derived from fractal geometry like the Julia or Mandelbrot sets, produce asymmetrical readouts20. A trajectory constrained to the positive quadrant of a terrain will produce a signal with massive DC bias. Furthermore, a trajectory navigating flat regions will produce near-silence, while intersecting dense topological oscillations produces extreme amplitude peaks17. To stabilize the signal, the processing chain must implement a high-pass filter (often a Butterworth filter tuned to 10-20 Hz) to center the waveform, followed by a responsive balancing algorithm or lookahead limiter to constrain amplitude variations20.

#### **1.4.3 Recursive Feedback and Spatial Compression**

Aaron Anderson introduced a trajectory feedback loop wherein the current spatial position is fed back into the calculation of the subsequent coordinate, a process conceptually analogous to audio-rate phase modulation2. While this severely distorts the trajectory to generate aggressive harmonic sidebands, applying positive feedback to a 2D Cartesian plane rapidly causes the ![][image15] and ![][image16] values to accelerate toward infinity. To constrain this "feedback explosion," Anderson employs a Spatial Compressor6. Rather than compressing the audio amplitude (![][image4]), the spatial compressor monitors the Euclidean magnitude of the coordinate vector, calculated as ![][image17]. If ![][image18] exceeds a maximum threshold, a gain reduction scalar is applied equally to ![][image15] and ![][image16], preserving the orbital angle while strictly bounding the maximum distance from the origin2.

### **1.5 Apple Silicon and Accelerate Framework Optimization**

For Latticewake to evaluate per-sample WT mathematics efficiently on macOS, it must leverage the specific architectural capabilities of Apple Silicon (M-series processors).  
ARM architectures utilize the NEON SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) extension, which provides 32 128-bit vector registers21. By utilizing the float32x4\_t data type, the CPU can execute four 32-bit floating-point operations simultaneously in a single clock cycle21. Critical to DSP performance is the Fused Multiply-Accumulate (FMA) instruction (vfmaq\_f32), which computes ![][image19] with a single rounding step22.  
Apple abstracts these low-level intrinsics via the Accelerate framework, providing a C API for high-performance mathematics.

> * **vForce:** This sub-library provides vectorized transcendental and trigonometric functions23. Functions such as vvsinf, vvcosf, and vvlogf allow the instrument to process entire blocks of trajectory phases concurrently, operating 5 to 10 times faster than calling std::sin() in a scalar loop24.  
> * **vDSP:** This sub-library handles signal processing routines, including vector-scalar multiplication (vDSP\_vsmul)25. Crucially, vDSP\_biquad executes cascaded direct-form infinite impulse response (IIR) filters27. Initialized via vDSP\_biquad\_CreateSetup, this function is essential for implementing highly efficient DC-blocking high-pass filters and the steep anti-aliasing decimation filters required during oversampling27.

Real-time audio processing on ARM NEON demands strict adherence to thread-safety protocols to prevent CPU spikes and audio dropouts30. Mutex locks and heap allocations must be entirely avoided within the audio callback31. State changes must be managed via std::atomic variables or lock-free ring buffers31. Furthermore, IIR filters and recursive feedback loops can produce denormalized floating-point numbers (values extremely close to zero). Processing denormals heavily degrades CPU performance; therefore, the DSP kernel must enable Flush-To-Zero (FTZ) and Denormals-Are-Zero (DAZ) hardware flags on the NEON registers32.

### **1.6 Intellectual Property Law and Cleanroom Protocol**

The legal boundaries of software development directly impact the architecture of Latticewake. Existing modern implementations like Terrain (GPL-3.0) and Image-In (LGPL-3.0) utilize licenses that possess a viral nature; linking their code or directly copying their source files into Latticewake would legally require the Latticewake core to adopt the same open-source license6.  
However, 17 U.S.C. § 102(b) of the United States Copyright Act explicitly states that copyright protection does not extend to ideas, procedures, processes, systems, or methods of operation36. Copyright strictly protects the *expression* of the idea (the literal code syntax)38. In the landmark ruling *Sega Enterprises Ltd. v. Accolade, Inc.*, 977 F.2d 1510 (9th Cir. 1992), the court established that reverse engineering a copyrighted software program to extract unprotected functional specifications constitutes fair use39.  
To safely replicate specific functional behaviors (such as the mathematical logic of Anderson's Meanderance or Spatial Compressor) without infringing on the GPL license, Latticewake must employ a Cleanroom Software Engineering protocol35.

> 1. **Analysis (Team A):** A primary researcher inspects the GPL source code and software behavior to extract the mathematical procedures. Team A produces a functional specification document detailing the formulas and logic flow without including any original source code42.  
> 2. **Implementation (Team B):** A developer or development team who has *never* viewed the GPL source code writes the Latticewake C++ architecture strictly from Team A's functional specification42. This protocol guarantees that the Latticewake codebase shares no expressive lineage with the original software, insulating proprietary or differently-licensed code from GPL contamination35.

### **1.9 DSP Failure-Mode Matrix**

| Failure Mode | Root Cause in WT Synthesis | DSP Mitigation Strategy |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Fold-Over Aliasing** | High-frequency trajectory scanning across sharp terrain gradients generating untracked harmonics. | Minimum 4x Oversampling combined with phase-linear decimation filtering6. |
| **Feedback Explosion** | Unbounded recursive coordinate modulation leading to infinite vector lengths. | Spatial Compressor applying scalar magnitude reduction to ![][image20] coordinates8. |
| **Severe DC Offset** | Asymmetrical terrain traversal (e.g., Julia Set evaluation limited to a single quadrant). | Cascaded vDSP\_biquad high-pass filters at 20Hz applied to the voice output20. |
| **Stair-Step / Quantization Noise** | Nearest-neighbor pixel fetching from discrete image/table buffers. | Bicubic interpolation (4x4 matrix) ensuring continuous first-derivatives18. |
| **CPU Spikes / Audio Dropouts** | Mutex locks in RT thread, dynamic heap allocation, or denormal floats entering IIR paths. | Lock-free atomics, pre-allocated vectors, enabling FTZ/DAZ on ARM NEON registers31. |

## **2\. Inferences and Open Questions**

The following section separates strict factual evidence from derived technical inferences, identifying architectural bottlenecks and open research questions for the Latticewake project.

### **2.1 Inferences on Apple Silicon Pipeline Bottlenecks**

While per-sample mathematical evaluation of WT functions appears computationally heavy, modern ARM NEON architecture and the vForce trigonometric sub-library are hyper-optimized for continuous ALU operations21. Conversely, scanning a 2D image buffer requires fetching non-sequential memory addresses, defeating CPU cache prediction algorithms. Furthermore, applying ![][image13] bicubic interpolation for every sample across a polyphonic, 16x oversampled engine requires massive memory bandwidth18. **Inference:** It is highly probable that a mathematical terrain engine utilizing SIMD FMA instructions will exhibit lower CPU utilization and greater real-time stability on an M1/M2/M3 chip than a buffer-based image-scanning engine of equivalent oversampling quality.

### **2.2 Inferences on Trajectory Aliasing**

While terrain gradients are the primary cause of fold-over aliasing, the modulation of the trajectory itself—specifically through recursive feedback—acts mathematically as spatial phase-modulation2. **Inference:** Intense trajectory feedback will generate high-frequency sidebands that exceed the Nyquist limit even faster than the topographical complexity of the terrain itself. Consequently, any preset utilizing heavy feedback will require maximum oversampling, regardless of the terrain's native smoothness.

### **2.3 Open Questions**

> 1. **Dynamic Oversampling Heuristics:** Can the Latticewake DSP engine implement a dynamic oversampling heuristic? Instead of a fixed 16x rate, could the engine scale from 2x to 16x in real-time by analyzing the highest mathematical derivative of the current terrain topology and the magnitude of trajectory feedback, thereby conserving CPU cycles during periods of smooth traversal?  
> 2. **MTS-ESP Tuning Interaction:** Microtonal systems like ODDSound's MTS-ESP adjust the fundamental frequency of the oscillator with extreme precision44. When evaluating discrete pixel boundaries in buffered image terrains, will precise microtonal ratios experience phase jitter due to spatial quantization and interpolation artifacts?  
> 3. **Bicubic Kernel Tuning:** The bicubic convolution kernel parameter (![][image21]) dictates the amount of edge overshoot18. Can ![][image21] be exposed to the user as a timbral control, essentially acting as an exciter or resonance parameter at the edges of steep waveforms?

## **3\. Implementation-Ready Recommendations**

The following section synthesizes the research into actionable architectural proposals, API designs, and mathematical kernels tailored for a native macOS C++ implementation.

### **3.1 Design Reuse Boundaries and Intellectual Property**

When examining open-source software like Terrain or Image-In, the engineering team must enforce a strict cleanroom boundary to protect Latticewake's proprietary licensing.

> * **Concepts Freely Reusable:** General WT synthesis mechanics, the use of elliptical trajectory readers (as seen in Image-In), MTS-ESP API integrations, mapping coordinates to 1D buffers (as in SuperCollider), and standard math functions (Julia sets, bicubic matrices). These concepts exist in the public domain or utilize permissive APIs1.  
> * **Requires Cleanroom Translation:** Specific logical implementations, such as Anderson's Meanderance vectors and Spatial Compressor logic. Team A must extract the algorithm mathematically (e.g., "detect vector ![][image18], apply inverse gain scalar if ![][image22]") into a specification document. Team B must implement this using Apple Accelerate functions6.  
> * **Strictly Prohibited:** Viewing the specific GPL/LGPL .cpp or .h files to copy variable structures, line-by-line logic, or directly linking the open-source libraries into the Latticewake build system35.

### **3.2 Portable API Proposal: TerrainField, Trajectory, and TerrainVoice**

To optimize memory locality and SIMD execution on Apple Silicon, Latticewake should utilize a modular, block-based C++ abstraction. Evaluating in blocks (rather than sample-by-sample) is mandatory to utilize vForce and vDSP vectorized routines effectively24.

C++  
// 1\. TerrainField: Manages topological data or math function evaluation  
class TerrainField {  
public:  
    virtual \~TerrainField() \= default;  
      
    // Evaluates a pre-allocated block of coordinates for SIMD optimization  
    // Uses vForce and NEON intrinsics internally for maximum throughput  
    virtual void evaluateBlock(const float\* xCoords, const float\* yCoords,   
                               float\* zOut, size\_t numFrames) \= 0;  
};

// 2\. Trajectory: Manages orbital path generation and feedback constraints  
class Trajectory {  
public:  
    // Generates 2D path based on fundamental frequency, phase, and drift  
    virtual void generatePath(float frequency, float phaseOffset,   
                              float\* xOut, float\* yOut, size\_t numFrames) \= 0;  
                                
    // Executes spatial compression using vDSP vector-scalar operations  
    virtual void applySpatialCompressor(float\* xBlock, float\* yBlock,   
                                        float maxRadius, size\_t numFrames) \= 0;  
};

// 3\. TerrainVoice: Manages polyphony, oversampling, and real-time execution  
class TerrainVoice {  
private:  
    Trajectory\* trajectory;  
    TerrainField\* terrain;  
    vDSP\_biquad\_Setup dcBlocker; // Apple Accelerate cascaded IIR setup  
    vDSP\_biquad\_Setup aaFilter;  // Anti-aliasing decimation filter  
    float currentOversampleFactor;

public:  
    // Lock-free render loop called by the audio thread  
    void renderNextBlock(float\* outputBuffer, size\_t numFrames) {  
        // Calculate oversampled frame count  
        size\_t osFrames \= numFrames \* currentOversampleFactor;  
          
        // 1\. Generate trajectory path into pre-allocated SIMD buffers  
        trajectory-\>generatePath(baseFreq, currentPhase, xBuf, yBuf, osFrames);  
          
        // 2\. Evaluate terrain at path coordinates  
        terrain-\>evaluateBlock(xBuf, yBuf, zBuf, osFrames);  
          
        // 3\. Apply vDSP Biquad for DC Blocking (20Hz)  
        vDSP\_biquad(dcBlocker, dcDelayState, zBuf, 1, filteredBuf, 1, osFrames);  
          
        // 4\. Apply vDSP Biquad for Anti-Aliasing Low-Pass  
        vDSP\_biquad(aaFilter, aaDelayState, filteredBuf, 1, aaBuf, 1, osFrames);  
          
        // 5\. Decimate and copy to host outputBuffer  
        // (Implementation omits scalar loops in favor of vDSP strides)  
    }  
};

### **3.3 A Safe First Kernel for Dynamic Mandelbrot/Julia-Style Fields**

Fractals like the Mandelbrot and Julia sets provide mathematically infinite, non-repeating terrains ideal for generative wave synthesis20. However, the standard implementation iterates ![][image23] until the magnitude escapes a radius (![][image24]), returning the integer count ![][image25]. This discrete integer step creates harsh, staircase-like topologies that generate immense quantization noise20.  
**Recommendation for Implementation:**  
To create a high-fidelity, alias-reduced topology suitable for audio, Latticewake must implement a Continuous Potential (Smooth Escape Count) algorithm.

> 1. Iterate the quadratic map ![][image23].  
> 2. Upon escaping the radius (![][image26]), calculate the fractional smooth value:  
>    ![][image27]  
> 3. The value ![][image28] represents a continuous gradient. This float value is then wrapped, normalized, and mapped directly to the ![][image4] audio amplitude48. The ![][image29] calculations should be executed across the coordinate block using vvlogf from the vForce library24.

**Real-Time Audio Thread Safety Precaution:**  
A trajectory coordinate may land perfectly *inside* the bounded set (the black areas of a fractal image), meaning ![][image30] will never exceed 2 and the loop will process infinitely. In an audio render thread, this will cause an immediate CPU stall and audio dropout.  
The kernel must enforce a hard integer limit on the maximum iterations (e.g., ![][image31] or ![][image32]). If the loop reaches ![][image33], the algorithm must instantly break and return ![][image34]. This guarantees deterministic execution times for every coordinate block, ensuring uninterrupted real-time DSP performance across the Apple Silicon architecture.
